chunks: Among them are the unlettered ones who know not the Book except as desires, and they do nothing but conjecture.

key_terms.أَمَانِيَ: Whims, desires, or what the soul desires
key_terms.أُمِّيُّونَ: Unlettered or simple ones, often referring to those who do not deeply study the scripture
key_terms.الْكِتَابَ: The Book, referring to the divine scripture
key_terms.يَظُنُّونَ: They conjecture or suppose, implying lack of certainty

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that the Ummiyyun know the Book only as amani?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse critiques the 'Ummiyyun' not merely as unlettered individuals, but as those who distort the Torah by mixing truth with their own whims (amana) and relying on conjecture (zann) rather than definitive knowledge. This highlights the distinction between superficial adherence to scripture and the deep, intuitive understanding possessed by the Ahl al-Bayt, serving as a warning against dogmatic rigidity devoid of spiritual insight.
